answer: A voyage-based reputation bond can resist sybil attacks: each agent identity must stake a refundable deposit and build a verifiable history of useful work before gaining full weight — like a ship earning trust port by port. A wharf-style checkpoint verifies completed tasks and peer endorsements, so a fresh identity starts at zero trust. A gale of fake accounts would each need to pay the stake and do real work, making mass forgery expensive, while honest agents recover their deposit over time.
